title: Data Interpretation
source: MindSpark Grade 8 Aptitude & Reasoning | Chapter 6: Data Interpretation
subtopics: Calculating percentage change between two periods
Finding ratios, totals, and differences from charts
Inference questions: which category grew most, which declined
learningGoals: Extract exact values from bar, line, and pie charts accurately
Find the ratio between two categories in the same chart
Determine which category had the highest absolute or percentage growth
Answer inference questions by combining data from multiple chart elements
coreIdeas: Bar charts: compare bar heights; read Y-axis scale carefully
Line graphs: slope direction indicates increase/decrease; steepest slope = fastest change
Pie charts: angle or percentage given; absolute value = (percentage / 100) × total
Ratio: express as fraction, simplify; always specify which quantity is in the numerator

workedExamples.problem: A bar chart shows sales (units) for 4 products: A=200, B=350, C=150, D=300. What is the ratio of B's sales to C's sales?
A company's revenue was ₹40 lakh in 2022 and ₹52 lakh in 2023. What is the percentage increase?
A pie chart shows 5 categories with percentages: A=25%, B=30%, C=15%, D=20%, E=10%. Total value = 800 units. What is the absolute value of category B?
workedExamples.concept: Pie chart percentage to absolute value

onboarding.coachIntro: Data interpretation is the most practical reasoning skill — and one of the highest-scoring sections in competitive exams. Charts are not complicated once you know exactly where to look. Let's turn raw charts into easy marks.
onboarding.placementRule: If learner picks 'I have done this before', skip Exercise A–B and start at Exercise C.

mission.missionPromise: You will read any bar, line, or pie chart and calculate percentage change, ratios, totals, and inference answers in under 2 minutes.
mission.successCelebration: Data Ace badge unlocked! You extracted every insight from every chart without a single error!

microLessonPattern: Read and extract values from a simple bar chart
Calculate ratio and difference from chart values
Read a line graph and identify growth trends
Work with a pie chart to find absolute values
Calculate percentage change across two periods
Answer 2-3 inference questions about the same chart

rewardLoop.streakRule: 3 correct in a row = Streak Flame + 5 bonus sparks
rewardLoop.badgeRule: Complete all 8 exercises with ≥ 80% accuracy = Data Ace badge
rewardLoop.celebrationStyle: Chart bars animate to correct heights + confetti + Data Ace badge reveal

reviewLoop.practiceStyle: Reteach: step-by-step formula application with a worked example on the board
reviewLoop.revisitRule: Pie-chart absolute value errors revisited in Exercise H

beats.teacherLine: Data interpretation has one golden rule: read the scale first, values second. A bar chart is useless if you misread the Y-axis scale. Is it in units, hundreds, or thousands? Once you know the scale, reading each bar is straightforward. Let me walk you through a 4-bar chart step by step.
beats.boardAction: Draw a bar chart with 4 bars: Products A, B, C, D at heights 200, 350, 150, 300. Y-axis: 0 to 400 in steps of 50. Label the scale clearly. Point out the scale-reading step explicitly.
beats.checkpointPrompt: In the chart with Y-axis in units: which product had the highest sales and what was it?
beats.fallbackHint: Look for the tallest bar. B reaches 350 on the Y-axis.

beats.teacherLine: Now let me calculate a percentage change from a line graph. Revenue: 2022 = ₹40 lakh, 2023 = ₹52 lakh. Formula: (New − Old) / Old × 100. = (52 − 40) / 40 × 100 = 12/40 × 100 = 30%. The revenue grew by 30%. Notice: always divide by the OLD value, not the new one.
beats.boardAction: Draw a line graph with two points: 2022 at 40, 2023 at 52. Show the formula. Calculate step by step: 52-40=12, 12/40=0.3, 0.3×100=30%.
beats.checkpointPrompt: A product's price was ₹80 in March and ₹100 in April. What is the percentage increase?

beats.teacherLine: Your turn with a pie chart. Total students = 800. Pie shows: Science 25%, Arts 30%, Commerce 15%, Tech 20%, Others 10%. Find the absolute number of Arts students. Use: (percentage / 100) × total. Try it now.
beats.boardAction: Draw a pie chart with 5 labeled sectors. Highlight the Arts sector (30%). Write the formula and calculate: 30/100 × 800 = 240.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Using the same pie chart (total=800), how many students are in Tech?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Scale. Bars. Values. That's all a bar chart is. Master the sequence.

boardDemo.title: Reading a bar chart
steps: Read the Y-axis scale and its unit
Identify the tallest and shortest bars
Read exact values for each bar
Calculate sum, difference, and ratio as required
boardDemo.teacherLine: If the Y-axis goes in steps of 50, a bar halfway between 100 and 150 = 125. Interpolate confidently.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Name the scale unit of the Y-axis before answering any question.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Bar chart shows monthly sales (thousands): Jan=45, Feb=60, Mar=55, Apr=70. Which month had the highest sales and what was the Jan-to-Apr increase?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! April has the tallest bar at 70. Jan to Apr: 70-45=25 (thousands) = 25,000 units.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Identify the tallest bar first (April=70). Difference: 70-45=25 thousands.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: How do you read a bar that falls between two Y-axis gridlines?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Ratios in 30 seconds. Read two bars, divide, simplify.

boardDemo.title: Calculating ratios from bar charts
steps: Identify the two bars you are comparing
Write them as a fraction
Simplify by finding the HCF
Express as A:B
boardDemo.teacherLine: Simplify ratios before presenting. 200:350 simplifies to 4:7.

sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Bar chart: Product P=240, Q=180, R=320, S=160. What is the ratio of R to S? What is the ratio of P to Q?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: R:S = 320:160. Divide both by 160 → 2:1. P:Q = 240:180. Divide both by 60 → 4:3.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: What is the HCF of 240 and 180?

sessionFlow.coachHook: The slope tells the story. Steep up = fast growth. Flat = stagnant. Steep down = decline.

boardDemo.title: Reading trends from line graphs
steps: Identify whether each segment goes up, down, or flat
Steepest segment = fastest rate of change
Read the exact values at start and end of each segment
Calculate percentage change for the steepest segment
boardDemo.teacherLine: For 'which year showed the highest growth', calculate percentage change for each year — don't just look at the slope visually.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Say: 'Biggest absolute change ≠ biggest percentage change. Calculate both.'
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Line graph — exports ($M): 2020=50, 2021=60, 2022=75, 2023=90. Which year showed the highest percentage growth?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Calculate % growth for each year: 20%, 25%, 20%. The middle year 2022 had the most.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Why might the year with the biggest absolute increase NOT have the highest percentage increase?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Pie charts hide the absolute numbers. You have to calculate them. One formula: (% / 100) × total.

boardDemo.title: Pie chart absolute value calculation
steps: Note the total value given in the problem
Read the percentage for the required sector
Calculate: (percentage / 100) × total
Double-check: all sector values should sum to total
boardDemo.teacherLine: If the total is not given, you can find the ratio between any two sectors directly from their percentages.

sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Pie chart of 1200 students: Maths=35%, Science=25%, English=20%, History=12%, Others=8%. How many students study Maths? What is the ratio of Science to English students?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Spot on! Maths = 35/100 × 1200 = 420. Science = 300, English = 240. Ratio = 300:240 = 5:4.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Maths = 0.35 × 1200 = 420. Science:English = 25:20 = 5:4 (you can use percentages directly for ratio).
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Why can you calculate the ratio of two pie sectors directly from their percentages without using the total?

sessionFlow.coachHook: The formula: (New − Old) / Old × 100. Memorise it. Tattoo it. Use it every time.

boardDemo.title: Percentage change with different scenarios
steps: Increase: New > Old → positive %
Decrease: New < Old → negative % (percentage decrease)
Find new value given old value and % change
Find old value given new value and % change
boardDemo.teacherLine: Reverse calculation: if new = old × (1 + rate), then old = new / (1 + rate).

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Verify: if old=200 and % increase=15%, new = 200 × 1.15 = 230.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: A store's revenue fell from ₹5 lakh to ₹4 lakh. (a) What is the % decrease? (b) If revenue then rises 25% from ₹4 lakh, what is the new revenue?
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: A price drops 20% and then rises 20%. Is the final price the same as the original? Explain.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise F: Two Charts, One Conclusion
sessionFlow.coachHook: Two charts = double the data. Combine them to answer inference questions.

boardDemo.title: Combining data from two charts
steps: Read Chart 1: note values for each category
Read Chart 2: note values for each category
Calculate derived metric: ratio, difference, or % change across both
Compare across categories to answer 'which is highest/lowest'
boardDemo.teacherLine: Inference questions ask 'which department earned the most profit?' — you may need revenue from one chart and cost from another.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Say the values from each chart aloud before computing anything.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Bar chart 1 — Revenue (₹L): A=80, B=60, C=100, D=70. Bar chart 2 — Cost (₹L): A=50, B=45, C=80, D=40. Which department has the highest profit? Which has the highest profit margin (profit/revenue)?
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: Highest profit: A (30L); Highest margin: D (30/70 ≈ 42.9%)
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Excellent analysis! Profits: A=30, B=15, C=20, D=30. A and D both have profit 30, but D has revenue 70 vs A's 80. Margin: D=30/70=42.9%, A=30/80=37.5%. D wins on margin!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Profit = Revenue − Cost. A:30, B:15, C:20, D:30. For margin: divide each profit by its revenue. D=30/70 beats A=30/80.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Distinguish between absolute profit and profit margin.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise G: Read Between the Lines
sessionFlow.coachHook: Inference questions need thinking, not just reading. Combine, compare, conclude.

boardDemo.title: Inference from chart data
steps: Identify what the question is really asking
Determine which data points you need
Calculate the required value
Check if the conclusion matches any answer option
boardDemo.teacherLine: Most DI inference errors happen because students calculate the wrong thing. Always re-read the question after your calculation.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Re-read the question AFTER calculating to confirm you answered what was asked.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Line graph — company profits (₹Cr): 2019=12, 2020=9, 2021=15, 2022=18, 2023=14. In how many years did profit DECREASE compared to the previous year? What was the average annual profit?
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: Decreased in 2 years (2020 and 2023); Average = 13.6 Cr
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Mark each year: increase/decrease. Decreases at 2020 and 2023. Average = (12+9+15+18+14)/5 = 68/5 = 13.6.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: How do you calculate the average from a set of 5 data points on a line graph?

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise H: Olympiad Boss — 3-Question DI Set
sessionFlow.coachHook: Three questions, one chart, 4 minutes. Olympiad format. Go.

boardDemo.title: Full DI set strategy
steps: Read the chart fully before answering any question
Jot down all values you will likely need
Solve questions in order — don't skip
For percentage questions: always divide by old value
boardDemo.teacherLine: Fastest students read the chart once, write all values down, then answer all 3 questions without looking at the chart again.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Extract and write all values from the chart before answering.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Pie chart — Budget allocation (Total: ₹2400 Cr): Education=30%, Health=25%, Infrastructure=20%, Defence=15%, Others=10%. Q1: How much is allocated to Infrastructure? Q2: What is the ratio of Education to Health? Q3: If Education budget increases by 20% next year (with same total), what % of the total will Education be?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Outstanding! Q1: 20/100×2400=480. Q2: Education=720, Health=600, ratio=720:600=6:5. Q3: New Education = 720×1.2=864. % of total = 864/2400×100=36%.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: In Q3, why did we use 720 (original Education value) rather than 2400 as the base for the 20% increase?
